Using AI requires a higher level of abstraction capability. AI in LLMs form is quite recent GPT-3 is from 2007 and consultancy firms are still designing frameworks for successful LLM adoption. Plenty of jobs will not disappear but they will definitely demand a much higher level of productivity. Also note that although allot of jobs did not disappear they have been massively reduced in number, just thing that agriculture used to be the major world employer a century ago and now it is providing less then 5% of jobs on most modern societies. Another trend that will probably emerge is full remote work. Why do you need a truck driver to be physically present? Just remote control the truck, this will allow outsource of work and gain extra training quality data, besides non stop operation by changing the driver on the fly. Same applies for almost anything as humanoid robots can seamlessly be remote controlled. Automation has been a constant in industrial and enterprise processes, now we have for the first time a trend that is social automation.

One thing to help people land a fitness job is to ask questions during the interview. One question in particular is to ask the person doing the interview, "Can you describe some of the things you struggle with at this facility?" This gives the trainer an opportunity to describe how he/she can help improve those situations.

Depends on if you want to learn to make great software or getting good at your job. Your job, as a junior in my experience, is going to mostly be small tasks anyway. People always complain about AI code not being their code, when 99% of them got their start working on legacy software and reading other people's code. They then learned how to fix these issues with Googling. I actually think just vibe coding is great for a junior to get experience in seeing code they didn't write, learning how the system works, and making required edits to fix bugs. In parallel to this, they can then go about learning how to guide agents as they write the syntax in building out systems. All of this requires effot, but I do think it has a lot of potential for actually teaching juniors today.
